title: design: several workspaces
body:
## Summary

Design for **several workspaces** in the desktop app: separate libraries (for example Work and Personal), one active at a time, so a leak of one never includes the other. Docs only; no production code.

- Spec: `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md`
- ADR 0032: workspace identity in `.kaipu/workspace.json`, the list in userData, one active workspace
- ADR 0033: moving an item between workspaces (rename vs copy, verify, delete; `assetId` kept; tags remapped by name; collision suffix; crash journal)
- ADR 0034 (round 2): per-workspace setting overrides that inherit from an "All workspaces" level
- Backlog page `backlog/several-workspaces.md` (🔵 Proposed), its row in `backlog/index.mdx` and its sidebar entry in `astro.config.mjs`

Refs NIW2-370 — https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-370

Round 2 added the rows for 0032, 0033 and 0034 to the ADR index (`architecture/decisions/index.mdx`); round 1 had left it untouched.

`backlog/index.mdx` shows a large diff: the new row is wider, and oxfmt re-padded the whole table. Only one row was added.

## Decisions

All owner decisions (ten in round 1, A–I in round 2, both 2026-10-29, and round 3 on 2026-10-30) are in the spec's decisions table, now 25 rows. In short:

1. One active workspace, switched from tiles in the navigation rail; no combined view; captures go to the active workspace. (0032)
2. A workspace is an existing folder with `.kaipu/workspace.json`; a folder that already has `.kaipu/` is adopted. The list and `activeId` live in userData. (0032)
3. Migration: the current vault becomes the first workspace; cloud entries without `workspaceId` belong to it (named explicitly by `legacyCloudOwnerId`). (0032)
4. The cloud catalog stays per account; each asset stores `workspaceId` **on the server**. (0032)
5. Tags stay per workspace; ADR 0020's reopen condition is not met. (reuses 0020)
6. Move a finished item from the Library, the item page or an editor; same volume renames, another volume or any synced side copies, verifies sha256 and then deletes. (0033)
7. Switching is locked while anything writes (recording, export, GIF, screenshot, move); writers bind their folder at start. (0032)
8. An unreachable workspace is unavailable; an unreachable active workspace refuses captures and never falls back. (0032)
9. Two actions, **confirmed in round 3**: "Remove from list" and "Delete workspace" (`.kaipu/` to the Trash; media untouched).
10. Dependencies NIW2-394 and NIW2-398: already merged.
11. Switcher: 36 px workspace tiles in the 72 px rail (one click switches; right-click Rename / Show in Finder / Manage; "+" adds; "+N" past four), a status-bar chip, the window title, a tray submenu, ⌘1…⌘n only while focused. With one workspace the rail still shows the active tile plus "+", and the chip still shows (decision 19). (0032, amended)
12. Workspace color (tag-palette key) and optional initials in `.kaipu/workspace.json`. (0032, amended)
13. "Move to" (never "Send to") and "Saving to Work" on every surface, with the disabled states; the capture toast says "Saved to Work", a label with no move control (confirmed). The Record page line "Recording to Work · Switch" replaces "Ready to record".
14. Per-workspace setting overrides with inheritance; five overridable keys (confirmed); shortcuts always global; `uploadMode` override kept on the machine. **Ships in the first release of workspaces.** Reverses the round 1 non-goal. (0034, new)
15. Synced folders (Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud Drive) allowed in the first release of workspaces. (0033 and 0032, amended)
16. No Kaipu Cloud account per workspace, and no Drive/OneDrive API integration (out of scope).
17. Migration: additive, idempotent, crash-safe, downgrade-safe; no flag.
18. The Library keeps every existing filter, per workspace.
19. **The feature is visible with one workspace:** rail tile plus "+", chip, a one-time dismissible hint, and "Move to ▸ New workspace…". (0032, amended)
20. **Multi-select "Move to…" ships in the first release,** with a minimal select mode. (0033, amended)
21. **Moving a recording suggests moving its exports** ("Move all 3" or "Move only the recording"); a group move is N single moves, not a transaction. (0033, amended)
22. The migrated workspace is named **"Default workspace"**. (0032, amended)
23. Cloud entries of a deleted workspace are hidden everywhere, with "Assign to workspace…" in Settings. (0032)
24. **No combined "All workspaces" Library view;** it exists only as the Settings scope. (0032)
25. Sidecar read hardening ([NIW2-568](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-568)) is a prerequisite: hardened, not guaranteed.

The spec has no open design questions left. Round 3 closed all six (Delete vs Remove, orphaned cloud items, multi-select move, exports following their source, the default name, and the "All workspaces" Library view). The only unverified items are the File Provider behaviours in the Synced folders section, for a separate spike.

## Things the code contradicted

1. **NIW2-394 (#410) and NIW2-398 (#412) are already merged**, so the "wait" in decision 10 is over.
2. **The cloud catalog is a cache of server data**, not client data. `LibraryService.doRefresh` (`main/library/library-service.ts:78-93`) rebuilds every entry from the server and keeps only `lastSeenLocalId`. A client-only `workspaceId` would be lost on refresh, cache clear or a second Mac, and the null → first-workspace rule would then leak. So `workspaceId` becomes a server column plus one endpoint. Desktop upload has not shipped (nothing calls `/assets/upload-intents`), so this is cheap if it lands first.
3. **Locking the switch only while recording is not enough.** Exports, GIF saves, screenshot saves, the editor autosave and the media protocol all resolve the folder at write time. `RecordingWriter` resolves it at `create()` and at `finalize()`, and the hub resolves it again for the cursor track. The design widens the lock and makes every item address carry `workspaceId`.
4. **ADR 0003 says the editor never "moves" the original.** ADR 0033 amends that word: the intent is the export path, and a user-issued move is a user action. 0003's reopen conditions are not met. 0003's status row was **not** edited; decide whether it gets an "Amended by 0033" line.
5. **ADR 0021 (tag sync, not implemented) merges tags by slug per account.** It must be scoped per workspace before NIW2-368 is built.
6. Screenshots have no edit project (they are flat PNGs); their move set is the PNG and the sidecar.

## Review round 1 (GPT-6.1 Sol)

Eight confirmed findings, all docs-only fixes in `166d73ef`. The owner's decisions are unchanged. Each fix adds a "Failures this must protect against" line and a checkable acceptance criterion in the spec.

1. **Move recovery could delete the only copy.** The media rename and the journal update are separate operations. ADR 0033 now makes the journal phase a hint: recovery inspects both media files, checks identity (size, mtime, `assetId`, sha256 where known), and rolls forward when the target holds the media. A side is deleted only when the other is verified. Kill-test criterion covers every step, including the window between rename and journal update.
2. **Drag copies leaked bytes into the source.** The move now deletes the item's `.kaipu/drag/` artifacts (hard link and copy fallback) from a drag ledger, and is refused for 10 seconds after a drag of that item. Healing sweeps the source's drag folder before the final delete.
3. **An open editor survived a switch.** ADR 0032 defines the switch as a transaction: drain a per-workspace gate, flush and await saves, Save/Discard/Cancel for dirty editors, close editors and the detail page, clear caches, bump a generation. Main rejects stale `workspaceId`/generation with `stale-workspace`; the renderer discards late responses.
4. **A deferred toast Save/Annotate wrote to the new workspace.** The workspace is bound at capture start and carried through retained bytes, toast payload and editor source. The switch drops pending toasts and bytes.
5. **A paused editor save could cross a move.** One per-item lock (item lock, then sidecar lock) covers session saves, screenshot overwrites, deletes and moves. `flush()` joins an in-flight write. The existence/identity check happens inside the lock, and a queued save is refused with `item-moved`.
6. **A tag read and write could straddle a switch.** The tag repository is per workspace, captures its vault once per operation, tag IPC carries `workspaceId` and generation, and tag operations run inside the gate the switch drains.
7. **Filtering the catalog before `composeLibrary` shrank the account cache.** The list composes with the filtered view, then merges the association updates into the full catalog inside the cache's write chain. The orphan count is computed from the full catalog.
8. **`needs-source` claim for exports was wrong.** `probeEditing` returns `exported-only` without resolving `derivedFromAssetId` (`edit-project-probe.ts:35-37`). Chosen: document the current behavior accurately, move the lineage check to Out of scope and Open question 4, and add a criterion that a moved original leaves its exports listed without an error. No lineage check is added, because it would add a lookup to every list.

Docs build: `bun run build` in `apps/documentation` passed (347 pages).

## Round 2: owner decisions 2026-10-29

Pushed as `c0db3a3a`. Kaipu has paying customers: the owner accepts a large refactor but wants a small, safe migration. Each decision has a decisions-table row, failure lines and checkable `- [ ]` criteria in the spec.

- **A. Switcher:** workspace tiles under the logo in the rail, where one click switches, plus a status-bar chip, the window title "Work — Kaipu Record", a tray "Workspace: Work ▸" submenu and focused-only ⌘1…⌘n. I checked that ⌘1–⌘9 are free: every default global is ⌘⌃+letter and main sets no application menu. (Round 1 said nothing appears with one workspace; round 3 reversed that, see below.) The `Rail` needs a new header slot (`packages/ui/src/molecules/rail.tsx:189-193`).
- **B. Color + initials:** new `color` (tag-palette key) and optional `initials` fields in `.kaipu/workspace.json`, with defaults on read.
- **C. "Move to" surfaces:** Library header name + count, a new "⋯" menu on cards and rows (none exists today, `video-card.tsx:95-115`), the item page, editor chips, the export sheet, the Record page ("Recording to Work · Switch" changes the active workspace), the control bar, the capture panel and overlay, and the toast "Saved to Work". States: not connected, blocked during a write, cloud-only, dragged under 10 s, exports staying behind, not downloaded.
- **D. Settings per workspace:** new **ADR 0034** with VS Code-style inheritance. Five overridable keys; overrides live in `.kaipu/settings.json`, are validated, and unknown keys are ignored. `uploadMode` is overridden in userData per workspace, and shortcuts are always global. Every `AppSettings` key is inventoried in the ADR. The ADR 0032 non-goal and the spec's out-of-scope line are amended in place. The "master settings" are `userData/preferences.json` (registry) plus `userData/settings.json` (All level).
- **E. Synced folders:** allowed in v1. Kaipu detects them by path and labels them. Scratch files go to userData for synced workspaces only: the spec explains why not for all of them. Any synced side always uses copy-verify-delete, which meets ADR 0033's reopen condition, so 0033 is amended in place. Evicted files and evicted `workspace.json` are handled, conflict copies are detected and warned about, and the unverified points are listed for a spike.
- **F. Out of scope:** a Kaipu Cloud account per workspace, and direct Drive/OneDrive API integration, each with a one-line reason.
- **G. Migration:** rewritten.
  - Only `workspace.json` and the registry key are written, and `settings.json` is untouched.
  - `vaultDirectory` mirrors the active path on every switch.
  - An older version ignores `.kaipu/` files, because nothing lists `.kaipu/` (`library-vault.ts:105-115`), and it keeps the registry key (`vault-location.ts:70-80`).
  - A folder change made while downgraded is adopted on re-upgrade.
  - An unparseable `preferences.json` is never overwritten.
  - The server column is nullable, there is a fixture test, and the release ships with no flag.
- **H. Open question 6:** "All workspaces" as a Library view. The recommendation was **no**: it contradicts ADR 0032 decision 1. It stays only as the Settings scope. Confirmed in round 3.
- **I. Library filters:** every existing filter is kept, computed per workspace.

**New findings from the code in round 2** (spec, Things the code contradicted 9–15):

- **No item menu exists.** Round 1 assumed one.
- **Wrong lineage line:** a left-behind export's page says "Source recording was deleted" (`library-detail-page.tsx:163-166`). The copy changes to "…is not in this workspace".
- **Sidecar read errors re-mint the identity.** `LibraryVault.sidecar()` returns `{}` on any read error, so an evicted sidecar would get a new `assetId` and lose its title and tags. Only `ENOENT` may mean "no sidecar".
- **Fixed names in `.kaipu/` collide with media stems.** A root file named `tags.png` already addresses `.kaipu/tags.json` as its sidecar. `workspace`, `settings` and `tags` become reserved stems.
- **Settings are not read at start.** `recordingQuality` is read when the Record page mounts, and `showBrandBadge` is read live; both must be bound at capture start.
- **Overrides cannot go in `settings.json`.** `mergeSettings` drops unknown keys.
- **The control bar can be in the video.** The "● Work" chip hides while `showBarInRecording` is on.

The spec's Current state was re-verified on `main` at `16cd8d80`. #428 shifted `main/index.ts` by 14 lines, and the citations are updated.

Docs build: `bun run build` in `apps/documentation` passed (348 pages). oxfmt is clean on the changed files.

## Round 3: owner answers 2026-10-30

Pushed as the commit after `c0db3a3a`. Each answer is a decisions-table row, a failures line and checkable criteria in the spec; every open question is now closed. The app is at 0.x, so the docs say "the first release of workspaces", never "v1".

- **A1. Capture toast:** "Saved to Work" label only, no move control. Confirmed.
- **A2. Record page:** "Recording to Work · Switch" **replaces** the heading "Ready to record" (`record.readyToRecord`, `record-page.tsx:254`, `en.json:283`, `es.json:283`), it is not added below it. `record-page.test.tsx:191` asserts the old heading and must change.
- **A3. Per-workspace settings (ADR 0034):** ship in the first release of workspaces. Confirmed.
- **A4. Overridable keys:** the five (`showBrandBadge`, `uploadMode`, `recordingQuality`, `exportQuality`, `screenshotCopy`). Confirmed.
- **A5. Color + initials** in `workspace.json`. Confirmed.
- **A6. Changed, visible with one workspace:** the rail always shows the active tile plus a "+" tile, the chip always shows, a one-time dismissible hint ("New: workspaces — keep work and personal captures apart") is anchored to the rail tile and remembered in userData (`workspaces.hintDismissedAt`), and the "⋯" menu, item page and editors offer "Move to ▸ New workspace…" when no other workspace exists. Criteria: the hint shows once and never again after dismissal; a one-workspace user reaches Add workspace in one click.
- **A7. No combined "All workspaces" Library view.** Confirmed; Open question 6 is closed as decision 24.
- **B1. Two actions** (Remove from list, Delete workspace). Confirmed.
- **B2. Orphan cloud items** are hidden everywhere, with "Assign to workspace…" in Settings → Workspaces. Confirmed.
- **B3. Multi-select Move is in the first release.** Specified minimally (the Library has no selection model today): select mode, checkboxes, shift-click range, a bottom bar "N selected · Move to ▸", moves one after another with an aggregate progress and a per-item failure list, and a failure does not stop the rest.
- **B4. Changed, exports suggested:** the dialog says "This recording has 2 exports in Work. Move them too?" with "Move all 3" and "Move only the recording". ADR 0033 now says a group move is N single moves under the same rules, each crash-safe, not a transaction, and what the user sees when one fails.
- **B5. Changed, the migrated workspace is named "Default workspace"**; new ones still default to their folder name.
- **D. Sidecar read hardening** is tracked as [NIW2-568](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-568) and referenced as a prerequisite ("hardened, not guaranteed") in the synced-folders section, the criteria and the backlog page. The spike's unverified points are untouched.

**Calls I made that the answers did not name** (please check): with one workspace the labels ("Saving to …", "Saved to …", the Library header) show the workspace name, while the Settings scope selector, the tray submenu, the ⌘digit switch and the window-title prefix stay hidden until a second workspace exists; the hint shows to every user once, including fresh installs; select mode clears its selection when the search, a chip or the sort changes; a group moves the recording first and then its exports; an interrupted group does not resume; Stop lets the move in flight finish.

Docs build: `bun run build` in `apps/documentation` passed (348 pages). oxfmt applied to the changed files.

## Review round 2 (GPT-6.1 Sol)

Six confirmed findings, all applied in place to the spec, ADRs 0032, 0033 and 0034 (all Proposed) and the backlog page. Nothing from the owner's decisions in Rounds 2 and 3 was reopened. Two decisions are new (26, 27), and decisions 2, 7, 14, 15 and 17 are amended.

1. **P1, reserved-name collision in the migration and the downgrade.** A customer's `workspace.png` (or `settings.png`) already uses `.kaipu/workspace.json` (`settings.json`) as its sidecar (`library-vault.ts:92`, `:185`, `:227`, `:378`). The migration would overwrite it, and deleting `workspace.png` in the older app would delete the workspace identity. **Fix:** the new files are `.kaipu/workspace/identity.json` and `.kaipu/workspace/settings.json`. A stem cannot contain `/`, and a derived name always has an extension or `.assets` after the stem, so no media file can address that folder. I checked `origin/main` (`b577e778`): the only `readdir` calls are the vault root, `.kaipu/drag`, `.kaipu/tmp` and one item's `<id>.assets/`; the only recursive removals are `.kaipu/drag` (and its per-drag folders) and `<id>.assets/`; the orphan heal is a renderer hook with no folder access. Nothing lists, sweeps, prunes or deletes an unknown subfolder, so the folder stays. The "reserved names" rule for `workspace`/`settings` is dropped. `tags.json` stays documented as the pre-existing ADR 0020 hazard (a follow-up may guard it). New criteria: a vault with `workspace.png` and `settings.png` keeps both sidecars byte-identical after migration, and downgrade-then-delete of `workspace.png` leaves the identity in place.
2. **P1, thumbnails force downloads of evicted files.** "No thumbnail generation" was not enough: `describe()` hands out the screenshot's own PNG and `.kaipu/<id>.jpg` URLs (`library-vault.ts:158-165`), the card loads them (`video-card.tsx:62-63`) and the protocol opens a read stream (`media-protocol.ts:84`). **Fix:** `describe()` returns no image URL for an evicted media file or an evicted thumbnail (local placeholder), and `kaipu-media://` checks `SF_DATALESS` and answers 409 without a read. The explicit Download is a read in main (`workspaces:download-item`), so the protocol never needs an exception. I also found that the orphan-heal hook treats a missing thumbnail URL as an orphan and would decode the file, so it now skips items with an evicted file. Criterion: a synced Library with evicted screenshots and an independently evicted `.jpg` renders and every file is still dataless afterwards.
3. **P2, `settings:update` response.** It returned the persisted object (`settings-store.ts:182-188`) and `useAppSettings` writes it into its cache (`use-app-settings.ts:21`). **Fix (decision 27):** every renderer-facing snapshot (get, update response, changed broadcast) and every main listener (`onSettingsChanged`, `onSettingsKeysChanged`) is the effective settings of the active workspace; the All level is reachable only through `settings:get-scoped`. Criterion: Work overrides `screenshotCopy` to manual, an app-wide update returns manual.
4. **P2, folder overrides can change behaviour with valid values** (`screenshotCopy: "auto"` writes the clipboard: `auto-capture-policy.ts:49`, `capture-handler.ts:240`, `:258`). **Fix (decision 26):** overrides from a folder this Mac did not write stay inactive until the user confirms that exact file once ("This workspace brings its own settings: Screenshot copy: Auto … Use them / Ignore"). The sha256 and the decision are recorded per workspace in `userData/workspace-settings.json`; a changed file asks again; Ignore keeps the All values; a capture never waits on the sheet. "Cannot inject behaviour" is replaced by the precise guarantee. Criteria for adopt, sync-changed file, Ignore and an unreadable file.
5. **P2, the failed-save screenshot editor re-reads `screenshotCopy`** (`capture-handler.ts:253`, `screenshot-editor-page.tsx:140-143`). **Fix:** the capture's policy `{ workspaceId, screenshotCopy }` travels in `CaptureResult`, the retained quiet capture, the toast payload and the editor source; the editor never reads the setting for a capture. Criterion: change the setting between capture start and editor open, and the editor follows the capture-start policy.
6. **P2, one workspace with existing overrides.** The selector stays hidden with one workspace (owner decision), but overrides survive removing the other workspace and travel with adopted folders (`screenshot-copy-settings.tsx:22-23` reads the effective value and writes the All level). **Fix:** rows never infer "no overrides" from the registry size; a row set by an override shows "Set for this workspace · Reset", its control edits the override, and a row without one edits the All level as today. Criterion: override in Work, remove the other workspace, the row shows it and Reset works.

Line numbers in the spec are the ones on `origin/main` `b577e778`. Docs build: `bun run build` in `apps/documentation` passed (348 pages); oxfmt `--check` is clean on the five changed files.

## How to test it yourself

This is a docs-only PR. Review it by reading:

1. Run `cd apps/documentation && bun run build`; it should finish with "348 page(s) built". (I ran it on this branch after the round 3 edits: it passed.) Or run `bun run dev` there and open the pages below.
2. Open `/specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design/`. Check that the one-minute block (summary, decisions table, open questions, out of scope, failures, acceptance criteria) matches what you decided on NIW2-370. The **Open questions** section now only records how round 3 closed them.
3. Read **Things the code contradicted** in the spec. Points 2 (cloud `workspaceId` is server-side) and 4 (ADR 0003 wording) are the ones that change your decisions.
4. Open `/architecture/decisions/0032-workspaces-identity-in-the-folder-one-active/` and `/architecture/decisions/0033-moving-an-item-between-workspaces/`. Check that the rejected alternatives and the "Reopen when" conditions are the ones you would accept, and that the round 2 amendments (each has an "Amended" status row) say what you decided.
5. Open `/architecture/decisions/0034-per-workspace-setting-overrides/`. Check the inventory table: the five overridable keys, and that every other key is app-wide with a reason you accept.
6. In the spec, read **Migration** and the **Migration** block of the acceptance criteria. This is the part that protects the existing customers. Then read **Synced folders**, including its "Unverified" list.
7. Read decisions 19–25 in the table and the new criteria blocks (**Visibility with one workspace**, **Select mode and group move**, **Default workspace name…**). Check the "Calls I made" paragraph in Round 3.
8. Open `/backlog/` and check that the **Several workspaces** row is there with 🔵 Proposed; open it from the sidebar under Backlog.
9. Review round 2: read the new section above, then in the spec read the **Name collisions with a customer's media** failure, **Nothing lists `.kaipu/`, and nothing touches an unknown subfolder of it** (Current state), Things the code contradicted 12 and 18–22, **Folder overrides need confirmation on this Mac**, and the new Settings and Synced criteria. Confirm that `.kaipu/workspace/` is a location you accept and that the confirmation sheet is the trade-off you want.
10. Spot-check two or three `file:line` citations in the spec's **Current state** against `main` (for example `main/library/library-service.ts:78-93`, `main/library/library-vault.ts:169-175` and `renderer/src/features/library/components/video-card.tsx:95-115`).
